newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: More Dutch millionaires - but poorer, survey shows.
newsitem.headline: More Dutch millionaires - but poorer, survey shows.

text.p: The number of dollar millionaires in the Netherlands increased by five percent to 116,000 but the average millionaire became poorer in the year ending January 1, 1995, a survey released on Thursday showed.

The survey by Dutch statistics office CBS, based on tax returns and a CBS poll, said the number of millionaires was up by 5,000 and they were worth an average 2.2 million guilders ($1.2 million), 0.14 million less than a year earlier.

CBS said this reflected a fall in share prices over the period, which shaved some 0.03 million guilders off the value of securities investments, reducing the value of the average share portfolio to 0.23 million guilders.
By contrast Mr and Mrs Average were slightly better off, with Dutch households showing an average 2,000 guilder increase in personal wealth to 136,000 guilders over the 12 months to January 1,1995.
The biggest single contributor to personal wealth was owner-occupied property, which accounted for around 57 percent of total household capital.

The survey also took into account entrepreneurial capital, securities holdings and bank credits, but excluded pension and life insurance entitlements and costly consumer durables and antiques. ($ = 1.903 Dutch Guilders)
